knowledge_point.title: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3z &=-2 \\ x+y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Using the standard method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3z &=-2 \\ y-3z &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-2-3z \\ y &=2+3z \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the latter can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-2-3z \\ 2+3z \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=2 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{3} &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

 
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{2}-5{x}_{3} &=-1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=3{x}_{3}+1 \\ {x}_{2} &=5{x}_{3}-1 \\ {x}_{3} &={x}_{3},\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{3}+1 \\ 5{x}_{3}-1 \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix},\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}

M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{3} &=-4 \\ {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=5{x}_{3}-4 \\ {x}_{2} &=1-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} &={x}_{3},\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{3}-4 \\ 1-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix},\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y &=5 \\ -10x-10y &=-25 \\ 8x+8y &=20.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 5 \\ -10 & -10 & -25 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 5 \\ -10 & -10 & -25 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} \\ -10 & -10 & -25 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & 8 & 20\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y &=\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$  in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=\frac{5}{2}-y \\ y &=y,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{5}{2}-y \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3} &=-4 \\ {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=-6.\end{aligned}\right.

question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{bmatrix}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=4 \\ {x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=-6.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=4 \\ {x}_{2} &=-6-2{x}_{3},\end{aligned}\right.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -6-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix},\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
